newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Nov car market disappointing - industry bodies.
newsitem.headline: Italy Nov car market disappointing - industry bodies.

text.p: Italy's two major car industry bodies said a fall in national November new car registrations was disappointing and accentuated the negative situation of Italy's car industry.
Italy's November new car registrations fell 17.1 percent in November from November 1995, with the first 11 months of 1996 showing a fall in new registrations of 0.33 percent.
The Italian association of car importers, Unrae, saw 1996 new car sales as negative and estimated 1.72 million sales for the year. In 1995, Italian new car sales were 1.74 million.
Italy's car producers association Anfia said it was holding its estimate for the year at under the 1995 level, and did not see any improvement in 1997 unless fiscal incentives were introduced.

Anfia added in a statement said that the November figures were very disappointing, while there was an accelerating trend in price cuts and dealer incentives which had a depressing effect on profit margins for the car makers.
